data.name: Abyss Cave
data.detailed_description:
Background Story


Recently DarkStar Academy of Sciences discovered a colossal cave, they sent a number of researchers, but they lost all communications with them after entering the cave. To uncover the dark secrets of this huge cave, the Academy is putting together an elite squad to send into the Abyss, They are called Abyss Raiders. Each elite member will have access to drive a Drilling Truck Survivor designed by the academy. The Survivor has formidable self-repairing, ore extraction and production, and research and development ability. If in such danger or if unable to contact with the ground, the Survivors can also support their independent exploration and research underground. As expected, after entering the cave, they are disturbed by a strong energy. In a great shock, the members have fallen into a coma, and Drilling Trucks went out of control. You have managed to enter the deepest part of the cave, somewhere between tens of thousands of meters underground. But truck bodies are severely damaged that many functions can't work normally...

At this moment, you hear hurried alarms in a trance...

As a member of an elite squad, you penetrate into an abyss myriametres deep, fighting against unknown creatures. Survive and explore this huge underground world.

In this game, you need to design and construct Turrets in real-time to defend against continuous attacks of your enemy. Meanwhile, you have a Robot Assistant who will assist you in fights, collect resources, and maintain Turrets. You can develop weapons, gears and Turret Units, and use various weapons and ammunitions to explore the vast underground cave and search for relics scattered around. Finally, find out this underworld world and escape from it.

Game



Modular Automatic.--- It is a convenient and simple defense device. You can piece different modules together to make devices with different functions. As for Battle Turret, it must be equipped with weapons and ammunition boxes to function normally.

reviews.review:
"Abyss Cave" is a low key Unreal kitbash from China, it's 10 years old, wasn't finished when it was launched and still isn't now.  Yeah, it looks like a promising narrative driven FPS, but the golden rule comes into effect.

What's that golden rule of bad games?  It's simple... whenever developers can't work out how to make their own game assets and instead resort to plagiarising the work of others, such that the majority of their "game" is other people's assets (which are just meant to be used as placeholders and educate developers on how to make their own assets), it turns out they can't do the other important jobs of game development... like making a game that isn't a clunky pile of unpolished garbage.

Most of the assets look like they're from the Epic Games "Infinity Blade" asset giveaway... that happened in 2015, so it fits the timeline.

Taking this shovelware seriously as if it was a genuine attempt to make a game, it doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

There's no option to change the resolution and only minor graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The game assets, such as they are, are much higher than the general quality of the game and it seems apparent the developer has just plagiarised/kitbashed them.  Stock assets are just there to be used as placeholders while the developer creates their own assets for their games, but what happens far more often is lazy/unethical developers just throw a bunch of other peoples assets into a blender and put their own name on the horrible Frankenstein's Monster that results.  Like this mess.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

These flaws make this game fall far short of the professional standards we expect from a modern PC game.

Despite not being listed as Early Access, this game comes across as unpolished/incomplete and probably should be in Early Access.  Worth taking into account if you're considering putting your money into this.

I like to consider the court of public opinion when it comes to the reception of a game.  Most garbage games never get any players... for obvious reasons.  The developers here managed to pull off something startling... this had a peak player count of over 2000 people!  Here's how they did it.  The game was dumped into a dirt cheap IndieGala game bundle... the day after is when the players hit.  The fun part?  That only happened on one day.  Immediately after the bundle sale.  The day after that?  Back to zero players.

So what happened is the IndieGala customers got suckered, and at face value this looks almost like a real game, because of all the "borrowed" game assets.   So you can see why people would have loaded it up to try it out... and you can also see why they deleted it immediately afterwards.

Let's talk about price and what this asset flip is actually worth.  Is this significantly better than any of the 140,000+ genuinely made games on Steam?  Of course not!

Abyss Cave has the utterly unrealistic price of around $5 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.

For comparison, the $5 asking price for this game could get you games like "DOOM", "Ark: Survival Evolved" or "Dragon Age: Origins".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.
